items.title: Scott Yanow interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, October 22, 2021
items.q: So very quickly I went through and I loved Eric Dolphy

ctx.x: I was reading about from your website your experience of going to college with LPs and I really related to that. And your description, it was quite a leap you made in a short amount of time from Pete Fountain to John Coltrane and Pharoah Sanders. Can you remember how that music affected you, expanding your listening palate back then?

Remember this is like [gap]. 1970 is when I first discovered Dixieland, it was a local radio show, and I noticed in the Los Angeles Times it mentioned it, it was like 5 to 6 PM on an FM station, Monday through Friday. So I thought well this is happy music, I’ll see what this is like. And it took a couple of days and then I was addicted to that. And then about six months later I discovered Chuck Cecil’s Swingin’ Years and I got into the Swing Era. But when I went to college all I listened to basically was…

It’s so interesting you say that because I shouldn’t talk about myself but very briefly I went out to get my first John Coltrane record because someone said, “You should listen to him.” And I picked up “Om.” And that was not a great place to start for me, and I’m afraid it scared me off for quite a while.
